# A null test of one copy of a node a tab's panel loops over. The panel is one
# record of the strip's loop over its tabs, so `#mark[2]` is the panel's own
# loop's third copy, as every target but bubbletea keyed it: bubbletea's
# presence check put the tab's index in front of the copy's ("1/2"), and
# answered no copy present. A panel not selected is mounted all the same, so
# its copies are present before the switch to it.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// A tab's panel is one record of the strip's loop over its tabs, which makes
// no copies of what the panel holds: `#mark[2]` is the panel's own loop's.
component panes ui.node {
    var tab = 0
    var items = ["a", "", "c"]

    ui.tabs #strip(:selected=tab) {
        ui.tab(label="One") {
            ui.text(value="one")
        }
        ui.tab(label="Two") {
            for var item = items {
                if item != "" {
                    ui.text #mark(value=item)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

func testPresentInAPanel(t test.Test, c panes) {
    t.assert(c.mark[0] != null)
    c.strip.change(1)
    t.assert(c.mark[0] != null)
    t.assert(c.mark[1] == null)
    t.assert(c.mark[2] != null && c.mark[2].value == "c")
}
